entries.content: Kanto — the eastern half of the Japanese continent in the world of Pokémon; settlements include Pallet Town, Viridian City, Pewter City, Cerulean City, Saffron City, Lavender Town, Celadon City, Vermillion City, Fuchsia City, and Cinnabar Island.
Pallet Town — a quaint, countryside town located in Kanto; has no Pokémon gym; hometown of Ash Ketchum and Gary Oak
Viridian City — Gym leader is Gary Oak; gym badge is Earth Badge; located in Kanto
Pewter City — Gym leader is Flint; gym badge is Boulder Badge; located in Kanto
Cerulean City — Gym leader is Daisy; gym badge is Cascade Badge; located in Kanto
Saffron City — Gym leader is Sabrina; gym badge is Marsh Badge; huge metropolis; located in Kanto
Lavender Town — a quiet, somewhat eerie town located in Kanto; has no Pokémon gym; known to have a lot of ghost-type Pokémon; lots of scary stories take place here
Celadon City — Gym leader is Erika; gym badge is Rainbow Badge; located in Kanto
Vermillion City — Gym leader is Lt. Surge; gym badge is Thunder Badge; located in Kanto
Fuchsia City — Gym leader is Janine; gym badge is Soul Badge; located in Kanto
Cinnabar Island — Gym leader is Blaine; gym badge is Volcano Badge; located on an island south of Kanto

Johto — the western half of the Japanese continent in the world of Pokémon; settlements include New Bark Town, Cherrygrove City, Violet City, Azalea Town, Goldenrod City, Ecruteak City, Olivine City, Cianwood City, Mahogany Town, and Blackthorn City.
New Bark Town — a cozy town built next to a river; located in Johto; has no Pokémon gym
Cherrygrove City — a relatively small but beautiful city; located in Johto; has no Pokémon gym
Violet City — Gym leader is Falkner; gym badge is Zephyr Badge; located in Johto
Azalea City — Gym leader is Bugsy; gym badge is Hive Badge; located in Johto

Goldenrod City — Gym leader is Whitney; gym badge is Plain Badge; bustling metropolis with a radio tower, a skyscraper that's also a mall, a casino, and an underground path with high stakes Pokémon battles; located in Johto
Ecruteak City — Gym leader is Morty; gym badge is Fog Badge; city has traditional Japanese architecture and two famous pagoda towers: the Burned Tower and the Bell Tower; located in Johto
Olivine City — Gym leader is Jasmine; gym badge is Mineral Badge; port city with a large harbor and lighthouse; located in Johto
Cianwood City — Gym leader is Chuck; gym badge is Storm Badge; small city on an island south of Olivine City; located in Johto
Mahogany Town — Gym leader is Pryce; gym badge is Glacier Badge; located in Johto; the Lake of Rage is a short walk north of Mahogany Town

Blackthorn City — Gym leader is Clair; gym badge is Rising Badge; old city with cobblestone roads and dragon decor throughout; Lance and Clair's hometown; located in Johto; city is named after the Blackthorn Family who founded it centuries ago

Indigo Plateau — the final destination for all Pokémon trainers that want to challenge the Pokémon league, they will have to defeat the Elite Four and the Champion in order to receive the rank of Pokémon Master
Viridian Forest — A large forest bordering Viridian City in Kanto; home to many Pokémon

Whirl Islands — mysterious islands in southwestern Johto that are so dangerous that only the most experienced Pokémon trainers dare venture there; legend has it that the legendary Pokémon Lugia is connected to these islands
Ice Path — an enormous frozen cavern that can be found on the road between Blackthorn City and Mahogany Town in Johto; houses many rare ice-type Pokémon; rumored to be the home of Articuno

Mount Silver — one of the most dangerous regions in both Kanto and Johto, this mountain range is on the border connecting the two regions and is known to have some of the strongest wild Pokémon around
Lake of Rage — a lake located north of Mahogany Town in Johto that is known for having many Magikarp and Gyarados

Flint Harrison — male; human; Gym Leader of Pewter City Gym; uses rock-type Pokémon; gives Boulder Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat him in a Pokémon battle; wife is Lola; has 12 kids including Brock
Daisy — female; human; Gym Leader of Cerulean City Gym; uses water-type Pokémon; is Misty's older sister; gives Cascade Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat her in a Pokémon battle
Lt. Surge — male; human; Gym Leader of Vermillion City Gym; uses electric-type Pokémon; gives Thunder Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat him in a Pokémon battle
Erika — female; human; Gym Leader of Celadon City Gym; uses plant-type Pokémon; gives Rainbow Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat her in a Pokémon battle
Janine — female; human; Gym Leader of Fuchsia City Gym; uses poison-type Pokémon; gives Soul Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat her in a Pokémon battle; daughter of Koga
Sabrina — female; human; Gym Leader of Saffron City Gym; uses psychic-type Pokémon; gives Marsh Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat her in a Pokémon battle
Blaine — male; human; Gym Leader of Cinnabar City Gym; uses fire-type Pokémon; gives Volcano Badge to any Pokémon trainers who defeat him in a Pokémon battle

Will — male; human; member of Elite Four; uses psychic-type Pokémon; has lilac purple hair; wears a maroon suit and a domino mask; personality is flamboyant and dramatic

Eusine — male; human; is a Pokémon researcher who dedicated his life to studying Suicune; has light brown hair slicked back with one lock falling over his forehead; wears a fine purple suit and white cape; good friends with Morty

The Burned Tower — a ruin in Ecruteak City that was once a pagoda tower; stands beside the Bell Tower; used to be called the Brass Tower before it burned down during a thunderstorm; three legendary Pokémon named Entei, Suicune, and Raikou perished in the fire but were resurrected by Ho-Oh

The Bell Tower — A pagoda tower in Ecruteak City that is sometimes called the Tin Tower; the legendary Pokémon called Ho-Oh can be summoned to the top of the tower with a rare item called 'Rainbow Wing'
Blackthorn Family — a prestigious family of dragon Pokémon trainers; they founded Blackthorn City in northeast Johto; Lance is the family heir; current head of the family is Aldric
National Park — a large park north of Goldenrod City in Johto that hosts a popular Bug Pokémon Catching Contest on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays.
Ruins of Alph — a mysterious ruin south of Violet City in Johto that is filled with various Pokémon known as Unown; contains puzzles to solve in each room

Ilex Forest — A forest in Johto that lies west of Azalea Town and south of Goldenrod City; contains a shrine associated with the legendary Pokémon Celebi; this forest is very dense and very dark but is not very dangerous
Union Cave — A medium-sized cave that lies south of Violet City and north of Azalea Town in Johto; a popular training location for young Pokémon trainers because it is not overly dangerous

Dark Cave — an extremely vast cavern located in Johto; it connects to Route 45 to Blackthorn City, Route 46 to New Bark Town, and Route 31 to Violet City; the upper levels have mostly weak Pokémon but the deeper into the cavern you go, the more dangerous it gets
Tohjo Falls — An enormous waterfall located on the border between Kanto and Johto, south of Mount Silver; a cave behind the waterfall is the secret lair of Giovanni of Team Rocket

Victory Road — a maze of caves that must be traversed by all Pokémon trainers who have 8 or more Gym Badges and wish to challenge the Elite Four at Indigo Plateau; these caves are full of high level Pokémon; there is a secret underground magma chamber that houses the legendary bird Pokémon, Moltres.

Seafoam Islands — a pair of islands in Kanto located east of Cinnabar Island; was once the home of the legendary Pokémon called Articuno until the volcano on Cinnabar Island erupted and forced Articuno to move to the Ice Path
Mt. Moon — a mountain in northern Kanto; located east of Pewter City and west of Cerulean city; features a complex cave system with mid-level Pokémon

The Power Plant — an enormous facility that provides power to most of Kanto; located on Route 10 just north of Lavender Town; most people don't realize that the legendary Pokémon Zapdos resides at the top of the tower
Sevii Islands — a cluster of nine islands, each one named for a number; Four Island is the home of Lorelei; islands are located in Kanto to the south; can be accessed by the ship 'Seagallop'
The Seagallop — a ferry that can bring people from the Kanto mainland to any one of the nine Sevii Islands

Safari Zone — a large expanse of land located north of CIanwood City in Johto; owner is a man named Baoba; features a Pokémon catching contest where trainers use Safari Balls to capture only one Pokémon, which are then scored by the Pokémon's strength and rarity, and a prize is given to the winner
Mt. Mortar — a tall mountain in the Johto region with a complex cave system; located on Route 42 between Mahogany Town and Ecruteak City; contains mid-level Pokémon

Sprout Tower — a pagoda tower in the Johto region's Violet City where a group of monks offer battles to inexperienced Pokémon trainers to patiently guide them and help them grow into more capable trainers with sound advice; a common stop on the beginning of a Pokémon trainer's journey.
The Dragon's Den — a cave in Blackthorn City that has a shrine to dragon-type Pokémon; only Pokémon trainers with permission from the Blackthorn Clan can train here; home to many dragon-type Pokémon
Pokégear — the equivalent of a smartphone in the world of Pokémon; has apps for making calls, sending text messages, taking pictures, listening to the radio, and a map.
